title_ar: تهنئة الشيخ الددو لفضيلة الشيخ النووي و جواب فضيلة الشيخ عبد الله اجدود " العباد *
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew's Congratulation to His Eminence Sheikh al-Nawawi, and the Reply of His Eminence Sheikh Abdullah Ajdud, "al-ʿAbbad"
body_ar:
قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو مهنئا الشيخ محمد سيديا (النووي) ولد سليمان ولد اجدود ترحيبا بابنه الغالي عبد الله، حفظهما الله تعالى

أعبد الله عش قرنا حميدا

كريما مكرما برا سعيدا

و كن كأبيك عالم كل فن

و للسنن المماتة مستعيدا

و للنهج القويم الزمْ و صنه

فعن وسط المحجة لن تحيدا

و للقرآن رتّل ذاك دأب

للابا كان دأبهم التليدا

حباك الله مما قد حباهم

و زادك رفعة و هدى مزيدا

و كن للشيخ ظلا و احو ما قد

حوى للطالبين فكن مفيدا

و سارع للمكارم و المعالي

و عش في ظله عيشا رغيدا

لنصر الحق فاسع و كن شجاعا

كأهليك الكرام و مت شهيدا

فكان جواب و رده فضيلة الشيخ عبد الله " العباد " بن سليمان بن اجدود مستشار وزير الأوقاف و الشؤون الإسلامية بدولة قطر على تهنئة فضيلة الشيخ الددو للعلامة النووية - حفظهم الله تعالى

السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته

حياكم فضيلة الشيخ وحفظكم وأبقاكم

منذ وصلتني القطعة الشعرية الرائقة الرائعة التي أرسلتم لي تهنئة ودعاء لابننا المبارك - إن شاء الله تعالى - عبد الله وأنا في غاية السرور والابتهاج بها.

وقد وقعت منا جميعا موقعا لا يعلمه إلا الله تعالى، وإننا لنعتبرها لنا من مفاخر الدنيا ونرجو أن تكون مما ينال به مدخر الآخرة.

وقد قلت أبياتا رغم تقادم عهدي بقرض الشعر، - ربما يكون ذلك أزيد من ثلاثين سنة لله الحمد - وأعتقد أنها لا توفيها حقها، ولا تكافئها في مبناها ومعناها، ولا تساميها في قدرها. والأبيات هي:

أعبد الله حظك لا مزيدا

عليه فكن به جذلا سعيدا

وباهِ محافل الولدان لما

دعا الشيخ الدَّوَوْ لك أن تسودا

وبالغ فيك تهنئة وحلى

ذويك من العلا عقدا فريدا

فجازه رب صالحة وضاعف

له عنا مثوبته وزيدا

وأعطه رب ما يرجوه طرا

مزيحا عنه كل أذى بعيدا

أيا شيخ الشيوخ وفخر عصر

حباه الله مطلعك المجيدا

هجرتُ الشعر مذ زمن وحق

علي الآن عودته حميدا.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew said, congratulating Sheikh Muhammad Sidiya (al-Nawawi) Ould Sulayman Ould Ajdud in welcome of his beloved son Abdullah — may God Almighty preserve them both:

O Abdullah, live out an age that is praiseworthy,

noble, honoured, dutiful and happy.

Be like your father, a scholar of every discipline,

and one who restores the sunnah practices that have fallen into disuse.

Hold fast to the upright way and guard it,

and you will never swerve from the middle of the road.

Recite the Qur'an measuredly; that was their constant practice,

the practice of the forefathers, their long-inherited way.

May God give you of what He gave them,

and increase you in elevation and in further guidance.

Be a shade for the sheikh, and gather what he has

gathered for the students, and so be of benefit.

Hasten to acts of nobility and to high things,

and live in his shade a life of ease.

Strive for the victory of the truth, and be brave

like your noble family, and die a martyr.

The answer and reply of His Eminence Sheikh Abdullah "al-ʿAbbad" ibn Sulayman ibn Ajdud, adviser to the Minister of Endowments and Islamic Affairs in the State of Qatar, to His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew's congratulation to the learned al-Nawawi — may God Almighty preserve them — was as follows:

Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

May God greet you, His Eminence the Sheikh, and preserve you and keep you.

From the moment the limpid and splendid piece of verse reached me, which you sent me as a congratulation and a supplication for our blessed son — God Almighty willing — Abdullah, I have been in the utmost delight and joy at it.

It has taken a place with all of us that none knows but God Almighty, and we count it among the glories of this world for us, and we hope it will be among that by which the treasure of the Hereafter is attained.

I have composed some verses, despite how long it has been since I last wrote poetry — perhaps more than thirty years, praise be to God — and I do not think they do it justice, nor match it in form or in meaning, nor rise to its measure. The verses are:

O Abdullah, your good fortune admits of no addition

beyond what it is, so be glad and happy with it.

Vaunt yourself before the gatherings of the young, since

Sheikh al-Dedew has prayed that you become a master.

He went to the utmost in congratulating you, and adorned

your kin with a matchless necklace of eminence.

So reward him, Lord, with a good recompense, and multiply

for him, on our behalf, his reward, and add to it.

And grant him, Lord, all that he hopes for,

removing from him every harm, far away.

O sheikh of sheikhs, and pride of an age

that God favoured with your glorious rising —

I forsook poetry long ago, and it is now

a duty upon me that my return to it be praiseworthy.

The served title has an unclosed quotation mark before العباد and ends with a stray asterisk, and the SEF slug is the placeholder '1257--q-.html' rather than a dated slug, which suggests the title field was truncated or mangled on entry. title_ar preserves the source exactly; the English title is given in readable form and the defect recorded here rather than silently fixed.

flags.arabic: فكان جواب و رده ... للعلامة النووية
flags.context: the prose sentence introducing the reply
options: read النووية as a slip for النووي and render 'the learned al-Nawawi', as done here
read it as an unidentified feminine referent and leave it unrendered
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. النووية carries a feminine ending where the person congratulated throughout is Sheikh Muhammad Sidiya, known as al-Nawawi. 'جواب و رده' is likewise awkward, apparently for 'جواب و رد' or 'جوابه و رده'. Both left as served in body_ar and flagged, not corrected.

flags.context: وباهِ محافل الولدان لما دعا الشيخ الدَّوَوْ لك أن تسودا
options: Vaunt yourself before the gatherings of the young
Boast before the assemblies of children
Take pride before your peers among the boys
flags.note: الولدان is the plural of ولد; in this congratulatory register it means the other children of the family and community, the newborn's future peers. 'Children' is literal but reads oddly in English of a newborn; 'the young' has been preferred. The line is addressed to the infant Abdullah, as the whole poem is.

flags.arabic: أيا شيخ الشيوخ وفخر عصر حباه الله مطلعك المجيدا
flags.context: the penultimate line of the reply poem
options: O sheikh of sheikhs, and pride of an age that God favoured with your glorious rising
O sheikh of sheikhs and pride of an era, whom God endowed with your noble appearance
O sheikh of sheikhs, glory of an age God graced with your splendid dawning
flags.note: مطلع is the rising of a star and, in poetry, also the opening line of a poem, so the line may be praising Sheikh al-Dedew's appearance in the age or, punningly, the opening verse he sent. The double sense is very likely deliberate and cannot be carried in one English rendering.

flags.arabic: قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو مهنئا الشيخ محمد سيديا (النووي) ولد سليمان ولد اجدود ترحيبا بابنه الغالي عبد الله، حفظهما الله تعالى
options: keep 1256 as the poem alone and 1257 as poem plus reply, cross-linked
publish 1257 only, since it contains 1256 in full
flags.note: OVERLAPPING RECORDS. This record reproduces record 1256's introduction and all sixteen lines of its poem verbatim before adding the reply, so 1256 is wholly contained in 1257. Flagged, not deduplicated.

translator_notes: Verse (nazm). Style guide section 4 requires verse to be rendered as prose in italics with the Arabic retained in the bilingual pane; body_ar carries the Arabic line for line and body_en keeps the same line division so the two panes align. No rhymed English has been attempted.

Genre: poetry, filed by the site under الشعر (Poetry). The schema's type list has no value for poetry, so 'article' has been used; the genre is recorded here and in section/category. The schema should gain a poetry type.

An exchange: Sheikh al-Dedew's congratulatory poem, reproduced from record 1256, followed by Sheikh Abdullah Ajdud's prose letter and answering poem. The second poem is Sheikh Ajdud's, not Sheikh al-Dedew's, and the attribution must remain unambiguous wherever this record is displayed.
الدَّوَوْ in the reply is the Sheikh's family name vocalised for the metre; rendered as 'al-Dedew', the form used throughout the corpus.
Mauritanian names are given in the local form; 'al-ʿAbbad' is kept in the quotation marks the source uses for the nickname.
No ruling of any kind is given, so the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload/publication stamp, not the date on which the Sheikh gave the answer. Records across this range carry timestamps clustered minutes apart on the same day (e.g. 1275-1278 at 09:51/09:53/09:54/09:55 on 7 March 2022), which is the signature of a batch upload. date_is_cms_upload is therefore set true throughout.
